findings.category: combat causality — assigned turn and win mechanism

draft_evidence.quote: The watch went east. Along the shelf, past the fire, in order, with the crossbows last and spanned and the empty-handed man last of all, walking backward the length of the hut before he turned

comparison_evidence.quote: the crews *herding the watch toward the line* — the watch will not step into ground where their own Paths die, and the crews who have walked into quiet ground three times and come out `[B7-OK]` will, briefly, which gives them a wall the watch cannot cross

findings.consequence: The scene says the watch has only one safe retreat, the Quiet line, but stages a different safe retreat and has the watch take it: east along the shelf. The crews never herd the watch toward the boundary; they step sideways off the approach into quiet ground while the watch keeps the shelf. That leaves the watch's ability to hold the approach intact, so its decision to abandon the post is not caused by the tactic and the required sentence at line 105 is an assertion about a fight other than the one on the page. Because this is the combat-primary chapter's assigned turn and resolution, the scene cannot safely advance on the current causality.
findings.repair_target: Lines 73–105 — restage the third exchange's positions and movement so the crews actually narrow the watch toward the Quiet boundary, the boundary becomes the watch's only remaining safe route/option, and the watch's break follows from losing the approach. Preserve the explicit fairness paragraph, the eleven-second nerve price, no declarations, no pursuit, and the watch's humane treatment.

findings.category: continuity — roster count and injury persistence

draft_evidence.quote: They went in at noon. Ten, and the healer of no Path, and Oryn, and Karis with the case, and the young one with the box; and the mule stayed at the hut with the fire, because a mule does not care about iron and would not have gone over it for anyone.

comparison_evidence.quote: ten = the crew's six (Karis included — a wall counts who walks a site, not who swings) + Teague's four (Teague and three). Healers are not on the count. Ch19's crossing by count must show the same ten (Karis crosses; the young one stays with the healers? — NO: the young one is on the count; the healers and the mule stay).

findings.consequence: Karis and the young one are already two of the ruled ten, so 'Ten, and ... Karis ... and the young one' counts fourteen people in a twelve-person party. The same roster also breaks during the fight: line 47 puts only seven fighters on the shelf, Seln off it, and Karis plus the young one on the crest; line 53 calls all ten advancing, line 69 still leaves the young one on the crest, and line 73 has ten through the barricade without moving the missing three. Finally, the broad man belongs to the ruled ten but line 117 says his leg cannot bear for three days, so the noon count makes it unclear whether he is forced to walk on it or has been silently replaced. A listener cannot reconstruct who crosses, fights, falls, stays, or enters the site.
findings.repair_target: Lines 47–73, 81–93 and 125 — stage the movement of all ten named-by-role participants, explicitly include Karis and the young one in the wall count, keep both healers and the mule off that count, and state who remains with the broad man after Oryn rules the leg non-weight-bearing. Reconcile every subsequent site-entry number to twelve total people.

concerns: TASTE — The exact completion-report mechanism remains one inference short of explicit. Lines 7 and 21 establish that someone with a sheet knew the route and told the post to expect six, which may be enough for a close reader; the card specifically says the watch was routed after the completion report. I would preserve the obliqueness unless the next chapter depends on readers naming that paper trail before its records scene.

TASTE — The narration sometimes explains a successful effect immediately after landing it ('a fight is drawn before it is fought'; 'a fight that can be said in one sentence is a fight that was won by a decision'). This is native to Cael's filing voice and not a tic-cap violation, but the causal repair should avoid adding more self-commentary around the turn.

SET-PIECE ANSWER — The barricade exchange is memorable: the cart-width shelf makes the brace unavoidable, the heel-to-palm frame makes Force visual, and the recoil climbs wrist to elbow to shoulder. The larger fight is not yet fully successful as choreography because the decisive terrain logic does not support the written win; F-001 is a contract defect, not merely taste.
The chapter is 5,070 body words, 220 below the 5,290 ceiling. Structural repair has room, but added staging should replace contradictory count/route clauses rather than accrete explanation.
strengths: WORLDBUILDING ANSWER — Yes: the chapter reveals the world through mechanism and use. Rust scale distinguishes old cordon from seasonal hut; fire seating exposes the watch's expected six; low tier is inferred from posting economics; the Quiet boundary changes courage and tactics; Tide healing spends the healer; carvings sit where a person under the Span would use them. There is almost no detachable lore paragraph.

The close-range Force acquisition is the chapter's best passage. Lines 57–69 reprise Ch17's planted feet, frame, contact, body's-length limit and wrist recoil, then escalate the price to elbow and shoulder. Cael is beside Teague for the whole exchange, so the thirteenth is earned rather than bestowed.

The fight's ethical frame is unusually clean without becoming soft: 'They're seven people on a posting'; 'Nobody declares. Nobody dies'; the watch's decision is called right; nobody pursues. Violence has medical and tactical consequence without gore, and mercy reads as competence.

The fairness paragraph at lines 77–97 protects the Quiet tactic from becoming a hidden superpower. Brom, Lira, Vastin and Teague each lose the named thing their Path supplies; the only advantage claimed is three prior crossings and the willingness to pay eleven seconds as bodies and steel.

Oryn's treatment scene preserves her independent competence and cost. The broad man's worsened limp, her quarter-hour depletion, the other healer's nod, and her refusal to let Teague hide behind 'Contract' all change relationships while staying in procedural language.

The Span reveal is disciplined: arch, piers, sink, inner-face carvings and bearing are discovered by walking and measuring; nothing new happens to Cael at the center; the reserved first-site feeling and every later reveal remain sealed.

The fixed closing log is verbatim, audio-legible, and performs several jobs at once: correct thirteen-item inventory, accelerated acquisition trend, Compact-knowledge payoff, oldest-last direction, and desire for the next site. It follows ch18's image closer with a distinct text/log beat.
